value.body:
Jack Heart, 2026-11-13, on the state-publication questions in scratch/questions.md. They were put to him as: (1) how an unchanged file avoids being uploaded again: a saves share content-named files under the state root, b each save is self-contained and unchanged files upload again, c add a copy path; (2) who deletes old saves when the worker cannot: a the launcher, b nothing, c a bucket lifecycle rule; (3) keep the previous save locally; (4) running_hours resumes from the save, as the docs say.

His answer, whole: "1b is fine, my other feedback was that extra stuff locally we can cleanup automatically is ok, but extra uploads are not".

So, decided by him:
- Each save is a self-contained folder of ordinary files. No shared content-named files, no manifest reaching outside its folder. This sets aside the "immutable files owned by the state root and shared by save manifests" proposal.
- Extra local copies are fine provided Etude cleans them up automatically (this answers 3: keep the previous save on the machine; retire older ones without the author doing anything).
- Extra uploads are not fine.

Not answered by him; my suggestions for reconciling "self-contained" with "no extra uploads", to check against the real carrier before adopting, and not to be recorded as his:
- Local saves and uploads need not have the same cadence. Save locally as often as run.save() is due; upload a save only when it must leave the machine (on the delivery interval and always before a stop). That bounds uploads without sharing files.
- Remote holds a fixed, small number of saves, not a history. One way that needs no delete right: two fixed remote slots written alternately, with the pointer published last naming the current one. Remote storage is then bounded at one spare save, which is the minimum any whole-or-nothing scheme needs, and question 2 (who cleans up under upload-only grants) mostly disappears. If slots do not fit the carrier, the launcher on the author's computer does the cleanup (2a).
- Within a self-contained save, a file whose bytes are identical to the previous save's is uncommon for training state (weights and optimizer change every save); do not build machinery for it.
- 4: running_hours continues from the save an attempt resumed from, as the docs say; the code should follow.

With 1 and 3 answered, state publication is unblocked. Specify the layout and retention rule in the docs, re-run both probes against it, then build the API in the order of "Remaining implementation". Stop at demo; publish nothing.
